note: Completed San Francisco projects with outcomes as published by the city's own evaluations. Quotes are tight and attributed; we never compute our own before/after, because regression to the mean, pandemic-era traffic, and small-n noise would make any figure we derived untrustworthy. Every sourceUrl was opened on the lastReviewed date.

projects.name: Safe Streets Evaluation Program, citywide
projects.what: Aggregated evaluation of 18 bike and pedestrian safety projects completed 2017 to 2022
projects.outcome: "Our findings show that street design changes are decreasing bike and pedestrian-related collision rates by 33 and 32% respectively."

projects.name: California Street Safety Project
projects.what: Road diet, intersection daylighting, continental crosswalks, longer crossing times, Arguello to Park Presidio
projects.outcome: "64% decrease in injury collisions in the year following project implementation."

projects.name: Tenderloin No Turn on Red
projects.what: No Turn on Red signs at over 50 Tenderloin intersections, fall 2021
projects.outcome: "On average, 92% of vehicles are complying with the turn restriction... Vehicles blocking or encroaching onto crosswalks on a red signal was reduced by more than 70%... close calls for vehicle-pedestrians decreased from 5 close calls before NTOR signs were posted to 1 close call after."

projects.name: Safer Taylor Street
projects.what: Quick-build lane reduction and intersection treatments, Market to Sutter; capital project completed 2024
projects.outcome: SFMTA's quick-build evaluation: the lane reduction "curtailed severe speeding on the corridor (30+, 40+ mph)" and intersection treatments "yielded higher rates of yielding to pedestrians by drivers and fewer close calls." Stated qualitatively by the city; no collision percentage published.
